images.title: Two lassi jugs in twelfths
images.purpose: Show the method cue for comparing and justifying: write both amounts in the same unit, here twelfths of a litre, then compare the tops.
images.composition: Two straight-sided lassi jugs standing side by side on one baseline with wide space between them, and one cue line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Left: one straight-sided jug drawn as a plain upright rectangle with a small handle, marked inside by thin grey #6B7280 lines into 12 equal levels; the bottom 10 levels filled teal #0072B2. Right: one jug of exactly the same size on the same baseline, also marked into 12 equal levels; the bottom 9 levels filled amber #E69F00. One thin dashed reddish purple #CC79A7 horizontal line across both jugs at the top of the teal fill. Centred below: one cue line. Exactly 2 jugs, 12 levels each, 10 teal, 9 amber.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame

any of the five question pairs or their rewritten forms shown anywhere
images.takeaway: Put both fractions in the same unit before comparing the top numbers.
images.description: Two same-size jugs each marked in 12 equal levels: 10 teal levels show 5/6 litre = 10/12 and 9 amber levels show 3/4 litre = 9/12, so the first jug holds more.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why both jugs are marked in twelfths before comparing 10 and 9.

image_decisions.why: The jug demo gives the same-unit method cue without working any of the five pairs.
